title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
summary: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.

title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
summary: Young people in Germany are preparing to protest over education and climate change. Politicians fear violence like in France, but an expert sees differences.

title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
summary: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
summary: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
summary: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
summary: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.

title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's PM in a political tangle
summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
summary: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
summary: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
summary: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
summary: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
summary: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
summary: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
summary: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
summary: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
summary: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
summary: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.

title: Nobel Prize in literature: How the winner is secretly chosen
summary: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in literature?

title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
summary: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.
